# Edit static LDAP roles

Update the static rotation period or replace the password for root-managed and
self-managed static roles.

<Tip title="Assumptions">

- You have [created a static LDAP role](/vault/docs/secrets/ldap/cookbook/static-credentials/create-static-roles).
- You have permission to read and update the role in Vault.
- For the GUI, you use Vault Enterprise 2.2.0 or later for self-managed roles.

</Tip>

You cannot change the name, distinguished name, or username of a role after
creation.

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

Use `vault write` with the
[`/<mount>/static-role/<name>`](/vault/api-docs/secret/ldap#static-roles)
path to update the rotation period. Omit `password` to keep the stored password:

```shell-session
$ vault write <mount>/static-role/<name> \
    username="<existing_username>"       \
    rotation_period=<new_rotation_period>
```

For example, to make the rotation period 24 hours for the QC role:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```shell-session
$ vault write ldap/static-role/qc \
    username="qc-tester" \
    rotation_period=24h
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

</Tab>

<Tab heading="API" group="api">

1. Create a configuration file, `ldap-role-update.json` with the username of the
   existing role and the new rotation period. Omit `password` to keep the stored
   password:

   ```json
   {
     "username": "<existing_username>",
     "rotation_period": "<new_rotation_period>"
   }
   ```

   For example, to make the rotation period 24 hours for any existing QC role:

   <CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

   ```json
   {
     "username": "qc-tester",
     "rotation_period": "24h"
   }
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

1. Make a `POST` call to
   [`/<mount>/static-role/<name>`](/vault/api-docs/secret/ldap#static-roles)
   with the configuration file to update the rotation period:

   ```shell-session
   $ curl \
       --request POST \
       --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
       --data @ldap-role-update.json \
       ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/<mount>/static-role/<name>
   ```

   For example:

   <CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

   ```shell-session
   $ curl \
       --request POST \
       --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
       --data @ldap-role-update.json \
       ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/ldap/static-role/qc
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

</Tab>

<Tab heading="GUI" group="gui">

These steps apply to root-managed and self-managed static roles. Your policy
must grant `read` and `update` on `<mount>/static-role/<name>`.

1. Log into the Vault GUI using a token with the appropriate permissions.
1. Open **Secrets engines** in the navigation.
1. Select your LDAP mount from the dashboard.
1. Select the **Roles** tab.
1. Select the static role from the dashboard.
1. Click **Manage**.
1. Click **Edit role**.
1. Update **Rotation period** without changing **Username**. **Role name** and
   **Distinguished name** are read-only.
1. Optionally, to replace the stored password, click **Enable input** for
   **Password**.
1. Enter the new password.
1. Click **Save**.

Enabling the password input does not retrieve the stored password. The field is
empty and optional, so if you enable the input by mistake, leave it empty to
keep the current password, or click **Cancel**. You cannot lock the field again
after you enable it.

On a root-managed mount, the edit form displays the **Static role** and
**Dynamic role** options but disables them, because you cannot change a role
from static to dynamic or from dynamic to static. A self-managed mount does not
display these options.

</Tab>

</Tabs>
